open_questions: High-resolution photometry/spectroscopy to measure rotational modulation vs transit shape and to break the low stellar-density fit
Additional Doppler monitoring and centroid follow-up once the star's variability is characterized
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 3.3 Earth-radius flat-bottomed dip repeating every 13.5 days on a small M-dwarf, with no nearby star able to mimic it. However the star's brightness varies at the same period almost as much as the dip and the transit duration implies a star less dense than expected. That pattern favours variability or a blended binary over a quiet planet, but follow-up is needed to tell which.

reasons.why: Phase-curve swing almost as large as the 13480 ppm dip signals flux modulation at the same period, not a quiet transit.
Low-density M-dwarf with a long, fully central transit implying a very low stellar density - classic spot modulation / spot-carved dip rather than a planet on a circular orbit.
